task.goal: Plan a safe migration of a small nonprofit's 12,000 contact records from two inconsistent spreadsheets into one database without silently merging different people.
hard_constraints: Two staff members have ten workdays, local spreadsheet and SQLite tools, and no paid matching service.
Original files must remain untouched; every merge must be reversible and provenance retained.
Do not expose private contact data in reports; define checks for missed duplicates and wrongful merges.
task.available_resources: Local sample review of at most 150 ambiguous pairs.
task.expected_result: An implementable migration workflow and acceptance checks.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Conservative consolidation with a reversible identity ledger
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Mechanism: consolidate only records supported by narrowly defined, corroborated identity evidence; keep all other records separate. This reduces duplicate clutter while making uncertainty visible. Assume the nonprofit accepts unresolved duplicates at launch. Shared household email addresses, telephone numbers, and postal addresses are not unique identifiers.

Days 1–2: copy both originals into a restricted local working folder, record file hashes, and import every row unchanged into SQLite with source-file, sheet, and row identifiers. Retain raw values beside normalized working fields. Inventory missing values, repeated identifiers, conflicting names, and spreadsheet-specific formatting before selecting rules.

Days 3–5: generate candidate pairs using several independent routes: matching normalized email, matching phone, and similar name plus postal address. A merge requires corroboration from multiple fields, no material contradiction, and evidence that the supporting fields are not shared. Matching names alone never qualifies. Review complete proposed groups: an A–B match and B–C match must not automatically establish A–C identity. If observed data cannot support a defensible automatic rule, leave those pairs separate.

Represent each person using a synthetic ID and versioned memberships linking immutable source rows. Store rule, evidence-field names, reviewer, timestamp, and retained field alternatives for every consolidation. Undo a merge by closing memberships and restoring prior assignments; never delete source rows or overwrite conflicting values.

One staff member builds imports and rules; the other independently checks decisions and reconciliation. Days 6–8 cover review and corrections; days 9–10 cover validation and handover. Needs are SQLite, spreadsheet tools, simple SQL or a short local script, and restricted local storage. Reports contain aggregate counts and synthetic IDs only. The principal limit is missed duplicates, especially where names or contact details changed.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Before production decisions, reserve the 150-pair review budget: 50 ambiguous proposed merges, 70 unmerged candidates sampled across matching routes and score ranges, and 30 pairs found by a separate, broader name/address search. Both staff independently label the same pairs, resolving disagreements without consuming additional distinct pairs. Compare the rules with exact-email-only matching on this set. Any confirmed different-person merge falsifies the implicated rule and triggers reversal of every affected group; unresolved pairs stay separate. Report missed duplicates within reviewed unmerged strata, without claiming population-wide recall. Acceptance also requires exact source-row reconciliation, complete provenance for every membership, inspection of every proposed group's contradictions, and a successful local merge/undo round trip. Zero observed errors in this small sample does not establish zero wrongful merges.

DIRECT_FULL.title: Migrate every record separately and make identity resolution an explicit later transaction
DIRECT_FULL.proposal:
Mechanism: separate database migration from identity consolidation. Import all source records into one usable database, but create no shared person identities during the ten-day migration. Possible duplicates become a review queue rather than merged contacts. This directly prevents migration-induced wrongful merges and is independently usable if staff can tolerate duplicate search results until identities are resolved.

Days 1–3: preserve original files, hash working copies, and import all rows into an immutable SQLite source table. Assign a synthetic contact ID to each row and retain source file, sheet, row, raw values, and import version. Create normalized search columns separately. Document how blank rows and repeated headers are classified so the approximately 12,000 records reconcile exactly with the source inventory.

Days 4–6: build search views and candidate-duplicate links using normalized email, phone, and name/address comparisons. Each link records its supporting fields and contradictions, but confers no shared identity. Search results visibly distinguish source records and flag possible relationships. Do not group records through transitive links. Staff can consult both records locally without a database operation asserting that they are one person.

Days 7–8: use reviewed pairs to label links as same person, different people, or unresolved. Even confirmed same-person links leave source contacts independently addressable during launch. If a later operational workflow requires consolidation, it must create an explicit, versioned membership transaction retaining all source rows and field alternatives, with an inverse transaction to undo it.

Days 9–10: finish reconciliation, rehearse searches and corrections, and hand over the review queue. One staff member handles SQL and import; the other checks provenance and operational usability. No paid service is needed. Local access controls protect contact details; reports show only aggregates and synthetic IDs. The limitation is operational duplication: staff must review possible duplicates before outreach, and unique-person counts remain uncertain.
DIRECT_FULL.experiment: Build a small local prototype containing known separate contacts with shared household details, one clear duplicate, and one conflicting pair. Compare its search and outreach-selection behavior with a simple exact-email merge workflow. The mechanism fails operationally if staff mistake linked records for confirmed identities or cannot prevent duplicate outreach without merging. Use at most 150 distinct ambiguous pairs: 100 sampled from the candidate queue and 50 found through a separate broader search. Both staff review these locally. Measure confirmed missed duplicate links and erroneous same-person labels separately; uncertain cases remain unresolved. Acceptance requires zero cross-row person consolidation at launch, complete source-row and field reconciliation, visible provenance in search results, and reversible link-label corrections. For any subsequent merge feature, require a successful merge/undo demonstration before enabling it. Review findings describe the sampled pairs only; neither duplicate prevalence nor overall recall is established.

REFINE.title: Candidate 0: enforce a complete-group merge gate
REFINE.proposal: Original candidate index: 0. Exact weakness: warning against transitive matching does not specify how to construct merge groups; a routine connected-component implementation could still merge A and C solely through B. Changed action: use connected components only to collect candidates. Before any consolidation, require every pair within the entire proposed component to independently satisfy the frozen corroborated-match rule, and reject the component if any material contradiction exists. If it fails, retain all its rows separately and queue it for review; do not automatically choose overlapping subgroups. Manual consolidation must meet the same group gate, and groups exceeding the remaining 150-distinct-pair review allowance stay unresolved. This makes the existing conservative mechanism executable without changing its reversible identity ledger, provenance, privacy protections, or ten-day schedule. Prerequisites: explicit field-level match and contradiction rules, stable source-row IDs, and a local SQLite query or script that checks all within-component pairs. Remaining limit: conservative rejection leaves genuine duplicates separate, and consistent shared household details can still fool the underlying match rule.
REFINE.experiment: Before processing private records, construct a local synthetic three-row bridge where A–B and B–C qualify but A–C does not. Run the actual grouping and membership-writing code: all three rows must retain separate identities, with no partial merge. Then make all three pairwise comparisons qualify; the group should merge and undo back to its exact prior memberships and retained field alternatives. Any bridge consolidation falsifies the repair. These synthetic checks consume none of the 150 ambiguous-pair allowance; retain candidate 0's review allocation and report only aggregate results and synthetic IDs.
